long_biography.plain_text:
At Almi Tankers, Costas Fostiropoulos treated shipbuilding as a long-duration operating decision. He instructed managers to plan for at least twenty years of ownership and to favour proven yards, environmental performance and future regulatory requirements over the lowest initial price.

That approach shaped the tanker company he founded in Athens. Its management system combined safety, environmental and quality standards from the outset, while investment in staff development supported a comparatively young operating team. Fostiropoulos also backed new construction during a weak market, pairing countercyclical investment with specifications intended for sustained service rather than rapid resale.
